speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Q Fever (Coxiella burnetii) infection.

The combination of sudden fever, headache, anorexia, fatigue, and malaise in a pregnant woman at 30 weeks, especially after consuming unpasteurized dairy products like ice cream, is highly suggestive of Q fever. This infection can cause acute hepatitis and poses significant risks to the fetus, including chorioamnionitis and premature birth. While I have requested initial blood work to confirm inflammation and liver involvement, the clinical picture strongly points to this diagnosis without needing further specific imaging at this stage. We will proceed with treatment to protect both your health and your baby's.
